dimensions.assessment: Involves federal agencies, U.S. investment personnel in Brazil, international financial institutions, and populations in the Brazilian Amazon.
dimensions.evidence: supporting Brazil's efforts to identify and disrupt the complex and transnational criminal networks contributing to the destruction of communities and deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes technical assistance, community financial support, and policy directives for international financial institution voting.
dimensions.evidence: provide financial and technical assistance to help prevent crimes by promoting lawful livelihoods... and the protection of rights

dimensions.assessment: Earlier versions authorized up to $10,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2025 through 2028, though the reported text authorizes programmatic assistance and reporting without specifying those dollar figures in the final text provided.

dimensions.assessment: Requires multiple federal reports, business development oversight, agency coordination, and policy instructions for international financial institutions.
dimensions.evidence: submit a report to Congress regarding certain drivers of deforestation and environmental degradation in the Brazilian Amazon

dimensions.assessment: Mandates annual reports for five consecutive years following enactment alongside ongoing diplomatic and agency coordination.
dimensions.evidence: annually thereafter for the following 5 years, the Secretary of State... shall submit a report to Congress

missing_information: Specific appropriation dollar caps in the updated bill text, as prior versions listed $10,000,000 per year while the reported version omits explicit numerical authorization limits.
importance_detail.rationale: Establishes reporting requirements, authorizes support for bilateral efforts against criminal networks and environmental crimes in the Brazilian Amazon, promotes sustainable livelihoods, and directs U.S. positions in international financial institutions.
